prov.heading: Section 19 replaced (Licences of certain persons subject to Mental Health (Compulsory Assessment and Treatment) Act 1992 to be suspended)
Licences of certain persons subject to Mental Health (Compulsory Assessment and Treatment) Act 1992 to be suspended

para.text: If a person who holds a driver licence (a holder) becomes subject to a compulsory treatment order that is an inpatient order or becomes a special patient under the Mental Health (Compulsory Assessment and Treatment) Act 1992,—

the person in charge of the hospital to which the holder is referred, or at which the holder is detained, must notify the Director of Land Transport of the making of the inpatient order or that the holder is a special patient (as the case may be); and
the licence is suspended while the holder is subject to the inpatient order or is a special patient.

If the holder has a physical driver licence, the person who has possession of the holder’s physical driver licence must, on the request of the person in charge of the hospital at which the holder is an inpatient, deliver the physical driver licence to the person in charge of the hospital, and the person in charge must forward the physical driver licence to the Director of Area Mental Health Services.
The Director of Area Mental Health Services must retain the holder’s physical driver licence until the holder ceases to be subject to an inpatient order or to be a special patient and then,—
in the case of a physical driver licence that applies to commercial vehicles, forward the physical driver licence to the Director of Land Transport; or
in the case of any other physical driver licence, return the physical driver licence to the holder or to the person who had possession of the physical driver licence under subsection (2).

In the case of a physical driver licence that applies to commercial vehicles, once the holder ceases to be subject to an inpatient order or to be a special patient, the Director of Land Transport must, as soon as practicable after the Director of Land Transport is satisfied that the holder is eligible to hold the licence, return the licence to the holder or to the person who had possession of the licence under subsection (2).
If the holder has an electronic driver licence, the Director of Land Transport may do either or both of the following:
prevent the holder’s access to their electronic driver licence:
amend the electronic driver licence.

Once the holder ceases to be subject to an inpatient order or to be a special patient, the Director of Land Transport must restore the holder’s access to their electronic driver licence if access was prevented and remove any amendments made to the electronic driver licence under this section as soon as practicable after the Director of Land Transport is satisfied that—
the holder is no longer subject to an inpatient order or a special patient; and
the holder is eligible to hold the electronic driver licence.
If a holder ceases to be subject to an inpatient order or to be a special patient and their responsible clinician considers the holder to be unfit to hold a driver licence,—

the responsible clinician must advise the Director of Area Mental Health Services of that opinion and the Director of Area Mental Health Services must give the Director of Land Transport a certificate to that effect; and

if the holder has a physical driver licence and the Director of Area Mental Health Services has possession of that licence, that Director must return the licence to the Director of Land Transport; and
if the holder has an electronic driver licence, the Director of Land Transport may do either or both of the following:
prevent the holder’s access to their electronic driver licence:
amend the electronic driver licence; and
the holder’s driver licence has no effect unless, in accordance with subsection (8),—
in the case of a physical driver licence, the licence is returned:
in the case of an electronic driver licence, the holder’s access to their licence is restored.
The holder may apply to the Director of Land Transport for the return of their driver licence and the Director of Land Transport must, if satisfied that the holder is fit to hold a driver licence,—
in respect of a physical driver licence that is held by the Director of Land Transport, return the licence to the holder:
in respect of an electronic driver licence, restore the holder’s access to their licence if access was prevented and remove any amendments made to the licence under this section.
The driver licence of a holder who is subject to an inpatient order or is a special patient is not suspended while that holder is absent on leave from the hospital if—
that holder is, under any of sections 31, 50A, and 52 of the Mental Health (Compulsory Assessment and Treatment) Act 1992, permitted to be absent on leave from a hospital under that Act; and
a responsible clinician certifies in writing that, in the clinician’s opinion, that holder is fit to hold a driver licence.
If subsection (9) applies—
in respect of a physical driver licence, the Director of Area Mental Health Services must, if they hold the holder’s physical driver licence, return the physical driver licence to the holder:

in respect of an electronic driver licence, the Director of Land Transport must, as soon as possible after receiving a certificate under subsection (9)﻿(b), restore the holder’s access to their electronic driver licence if access was prevented and remove any amendments made to the licence under this section.

prov.heading: Existing conventions include amendments to those conventions

para.text: A convention, protocol, or agreement specified in Schedule 2 as inserted by the amendment Act includes any amendment to, or revision of, that convention, protocol, or agreement—
if New Zealand is a party to the amendment or revision; and
whether New Zealand became a party to the amendment or revision before, on, or after the date that the amendment Act came into force.
In this clause, amendment Act means the Regulatory Systems (Transport) Amendment Act 2026.
